html:
The Temple of the Tooth in Kandy, Sri Lanka, holds a tooth said to be the Buddha's. A shrine for it was first built here in the late 1500s, and most of the present temple dates from the 1700s.

The relic is said to have reached the island in the 4th century, hidden in a princess's hair. Whoever held it had the right to rule, so it moved with the capital, from Anuradhapura to Polonnaruwa and at last to Kandy. The Portuguese said they destroyed it at Goa in 1560; the Sinhalese said they burned a copy.

Each year the Esala Perahera procession carries the relic casket through the town on an elephant. In 1998 a Tamil Tiger truck bomb damaged the temple.
